The estimated cost per avoided headache-day was less than half for patients treated with OnabotA in comparison with topiramate ($116 vs. $246). Sensitivity analyses showed that the incremental cost per headache-day avoided remained below $50 and the incremental cost per QALY gained remained below $100,000 across all tested ranges. Results were similar when using a lower, RCT-supported discontinuation rate for topiramate. In scenario analyses, a longer time horizon and a greater price discount for OnabotA substantially reduced the incremental cost-effectiveness ratios. OnabotA was a cost-effective preventive treatment of chronic migraine versus topiramate. Although OnabotA had higher drug acquisition costs, these were offset by reduced HCRU costs due to fewer migraines, resulting in a low incremental cost per headache-day avoided versus topiramate.

title: Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-67 Derived Nanoporous Carbon for Highly Efficient Effervescent Tablet-assisted Magnetic Solid-Phase Extraction of Clozapine and Its Metabolites in Human Urine Samples.
abstract: A novel effervescent tablet based on zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF)-67-derived nanoporous carbon was fabricated and applied for simultaneous analysis of clozapine (CPZ) and its metabolites in human urine samples coupled with liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS). Adsorption experiments and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis revealed the affinity of ZIF-67-derived nanoporous carbon toward the analytes through π-π, hydrophobic, hydrogen bonding, and coordination interactions. Meanwhile, this sorbent exhibited excellent exclusion ability against interfering substances in urine samples. For the construction of the ZIF-67-derived nanoporous carbon-based effervescent tablet, both the tablet composition and the parameters affecting magnetic solid-phase extraction were optimized in detail. The proposed magnetic effervescent tablet enabled a fast adsorption process (∼5 min) and provided enhanced extraction efficiency (87.4%-98.3%) in a simple and convenient step. Coupled with LC-MS/MS, the developed method offered acceptable matrix effects of 0.98-1.00, wide linear ranges of 0.06-3000 ng/mL with correlation coefficients ≥0.9990, low detection limits of 0.02-0.30 ng/mL, and satisfactory recoveries of 91.1%-99.2%. In addition, the present approach allowed direct loading of crude urine samples without additional dilution and filtration steps, significantly simplifying the operation procedure. These results demonstrated an alternative strategy for highly efficient and convenient monitoring of CPZ and its metabolites in urine samples and proved the great application potential of ZIF-67-derived nanoporous carbon effervescent tablets for extracting pharmaceuticals from complex samples.

title: Smart Soup Ameliorates Cognitive Dysfunction in Diabetic Encephalopathy by Inhibiting Hippocampal Ferroptosis and Restoring Mitophagic Balance.
abstract: Diabetic encephalopathy (DE), a prevalent complication of diabetes, is strongly associated with progressive cognitive dysfunction. The iron-dependent regulated cell death process known as ferroptosis has been implicated in the neurodegeneration observed in DE. Smart soup (SS), a classic Chinese herbal formula, is used to treat memory impairment. In this study, we evaluated the therapeutic potential of SS against DE. We found that oral administration of SS significantly ameliorated learning and memory deficits in a rat model of DE. This cognitive improvement was accompanied by the inhibition of hippocampal ferroptosis, evidenced by decreased lipid peroxidation, iron overload, and reactive oxygen species (ROS), alongside increased levels of the antiferroptotic proteins GPX4 and FTH1. Furthermore, SS treatment mitigated aberrant mitochondrial alterations and reduced the levels of mitophagy-related proteins (PINK1 and Parkin), suggesting it alleviates the upstream damage that triggers excessive mitophagic activity. Mechanistically, SS appears to target NR3C1 (glucocorticoid receptor), downregulating its transcriptional activation of key iron metabolism factors, LCN2 and NCOA4. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that SS exerts neuroprotective effects in DE likely by suppressing ferroptosis via the NR3C1/LCN2/NCOA4 axis and improving mitochondrial homeostasis, offering a promising therapeutic strategy for this condition.

title: Pre-emptive pharmacogenomics testing in clinical practice: A pilot implementation in Singapore.
abstract: Pre-emptive pharmacogenomics (PPGx) testing holds promise for optimizing drug therapy, but uptake remains limited in Asia. This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility of PPGx uptake into clinical practice and its impact on prescribing in an Asian healthcare setting. A prospective, multicentre pilot study was conducted to pre-emptively genotype 16 pharmacogenes. Results were integrated into electronic health records, alongside deployment of clinical decision support (CDS) tools for 31 drug-gene pairs. A pharmacogenomics drug information service and digital platforms were also developed. All 2492 participants carried ≥1 actionable variant (median: 5, range: 1-11). Across four institutions within one cluster, 1046 out of 2238 (46.7%) patients were prescribed ≥1 drug with pharmacogenetic association, and of those, 460 (44%) had genotypes linked to undesirable drug responses. Among 285 interruptive CDS alerts, 69 (24.2%) led to prescription modifications. Acceptance was higher for new prescriptions (50.0% vs. 17.3%, p < 0.001), in outpatient settings (31.0% vs. 7.3%, p < 0.001) and among consultants (57.1% vs. other designations 5-27.3%, p < 0.001). The drug information service received 137 enquiries, while 471 and 151 patients accessed the app and web-based platforms respectively. PPGx testing and genotype-guided prescribing are feasible in Singapore. Widespread adoption requires leadership support, robust informatics infrastructure, clinician engagement and sustainable funding.

title: Fetal Liver Volume and Morphology in Growth-Restricted Fetuses and Their Association With Neonatal Morbidity: An MRI Study.
journal: Journal of magnetic resonance imaging : JMRI
abstract: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) may induce redistribution of the fetal circulation to preserve perfusion of vital organs. Reduced hepatic delivery of oxygen- and nutrient-rich blood may cause volumetric and morphological remodeling. To quantify fetal liver volume and morphology in FGR and assess associations with adverse neonatal outcomes. Single-center, prospective and retrospective. Ninety-two singleton pregnancies: 36 FGR cases (prospective) and 56 appropriate-for-gestational-age (AGA) controls (retrospective). 3-T, True Fast Imaging with Steady-State Free Precession (TrueFISP) for fetal liver and body imaging, and TrueFISP or Half-Fourier Acquisition Single-shot Turbo Spin-Echo for brain imaging. The fetal liver, body, and brain were segmented using deep learning tools. Liver volume, liver-to-body and brain-to-liver volume ratios, and 12 liver PyRadiomics shape features were assessed. Neonates were followed for composite adverse neonatal outcomes (CANO) until discharge. Linear regression assessed associations with gestational age in AGA fetuses. Linear mixed-effects models compared groups, adjusting for gestational age and fetal sex. Univariable logistic regression assessed associations with CANO. Benjamini-Hochberg correction controlled the false discovery rate at 0.05. FGR fetuses had significantly lower liver volume than AGA fetuses (74.95 ± 1.76 vs. 114.89 ± 2.18 cm3), lower liver-to-body ratio (0.053 ± 0.001 vs. 0.057 ± 0.001), and higher brain-to-liver ratio (2.637 ± 0.085 vs. 1.978 ± 0.047). FGR fetuses demonstrated significantly less elongated liver geometry, (10.7% higher PyRadiomics elongation values) and had a significantly higher surface-to-volume ratio (11.9%). CANO occurred in 30/92 neonates (27 FGR, 3 AGA). Higher brain-to-liver ratio (OR = 4.12, 95% CI: 1.93-8.77), PyRadiomics elongation values (less elongated geometry; OR = 2.04, 95% CI: 1.26-3.30), PyRadiomics flatness values (less flattened geometry; OR = 1.69, 95% CI: 1.07-2.65), and surface-to-volume ratio (OR = 3.26, 95% CI: 1.80-5.90) were significantly associated with CANO. FGR was associated with reduced fetal liver size and altered geometry, which were associated with neonatal morbidity. 2. 2.

title: Network disruption in post-stroke depressive symptoms: a Bayesian multicohort study.
abstract: Post-stroke depressive symptoms are common, but studies on the contributions of lesion locations to depression symptoms remain inconsistent. Bayesian statistics offer the possibility to clarify these inconsistencies by providing evidence in favor and against observed associations. We reanalyzed four previously published observational cohorts with 1,864 patients with stroke characterized for depressive symptoms from France, Korea, Germany and the USA. We performed voxel-wise Bayes factor mapping using general linear models. Lesion maps were used to test for associations of post-stroke depressive symptoms with lesion location. Network level associations were tested based on structural disconnection and functional lesion network maps estimated by reference to normative connectome data. Due to a sample size with broad lesion coverage, Bayesian inference was informative in large parts of the brain. Lesion associations were found in clusters in the right hemisphere including cortical (frontal, insular, parietal) and subcortical regions (striatum, amygdala, hippocampus) and adjacent white matter. Evidence of no contribution to post-stroke depressive symptoms was observed in large parts of the left hemisphere. Structural disconnection was linked to depressive symptoms in the bilateral frontal white matter prominently involving the corpus callosum and anterior thalamic radiation. Lesion network mapping revealed evidence of an association of post-stroke depressive symptoms with network connectivity in the left posterior cingulate cortex and precuneus, and less consistently, the bilateral anterior insula, along with widespread absence of associations in other regions. Depressive symptoms were most strongly associated with right frontal lesions and right-dominant structural disconnection in frontal cortico-subcortical circuits.

title: The Role of Estrogen and Its Receptors in Brain Development and Their Long-Term Effects.
journal: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
abstract: Estrogens are a class of steroid hormones that participate not only in reproduction and sexual differentiation but also in brain development. The major endogenous estrogens include estrone (E1), 17β-estradiol (E2), and estriol (E3), whose relative abundance and biological sources vary across sex and life stage. During fetal and early postnatal development, estrogenic signaling is sensitive to both intrinsic physiological conditions and extrinsic environmental factors. Through estrogen receptor (ER)-mediated signaling, endogenous estrogens regulate neuronal migration, differentiation, and synaptic plasticity, thereby influencing brain morphology, functional development, and sexual differentiation. Dysregulated estrogen signaling may alter the development of sexually differentiated brain regions and thereby contribute to sex-related differences in brain function and disease vulnerability. This review summarizes the distribution and expression patterns of estrogen and its receptors in the brain, elucidates the role of endogenous estrogen and ERs in neurodevelopment, and examines the impact of exogenous estrogenic and endocrine-disrupting exposures on brain maturation. Together, these findings provide a framework for understanding how estrogen signaling contributes to neurodevelopment and its long-term outcomes.

title: Structural and EEG Motor Networks Distinguish Level of Motor Impairment After Stroke.
abstract: The objective of this study was to determine how structural and EEG-based functional connectivity jointly distinguish levels of motor impairment after stroke. We estimated patient-specific (1) structural connectivity using MRI-derived lesion models and (2) functional connectivity using source-localized EEG, guided by each patient's structural connectome. Analyses focused on the brainstem and three motor-related cortical regions bilaterally: primary motor cortex (M1), dorsal premotor cortex (PMd), and supplementary motor cortex (SMA). Network analysis metrics (degree centrality, average efficiency, betweenness centrality) were applied to structural and functional data, contrasting motor networks between patients with high (H) and low (L) upper extremity motor function. Structural disconnection of the brainstem from M1 and PMd carried the highest probability of low motor status. All network measures were elevated in the H group compared to the L group across motor-related regions, indicating a globally strengthened motor network organization associated with better motor function. Functional connectivity revealed convergent but distinct patterns. In the delta band (1-3 Hz), ipsilesional motor regions showed stronger connectivity in the H group. In the beta band (14-29 Hz), contralesional motor regions demonstrated enhanced connectivity in H patients, consistent with prior evidence that contralesional motor regions may contribute to motor function after ipsilesional injury. We also introduced a novel metric, motor betweenness centrality, to quantify the role of nonmotor regions in rerouting motor-related communication. Almost all new hubs identified structurally were associated with lower motor status, suggesting less efficient network organization in more impaired patients. Thus, preservation of direct motor pathways supports better motor status, while reliance on alternative, less efficient routes correlates with worse outcomes. By contrast, EEG routing revealed that H patients recruited proximal cortical hubs, while L patients relied on distant, inefficient ones, highlighting functional network organization not evident in the structural analysis. These patterns suggest that more local network organization, rather than more distributed rerouting, is associated with better motor status within the motor system. In summary, multimodal network properties reliably identified key motor ROIs predictive of motor status. This concordance suggests that EEG-based metrics, particularly delta- and beta-band connectivity, are associated with lesion-derived structural disruption and complementary features of motor-network organization. Structural connectivity damage within motor circuits defines the extent of network disruption associated with motor impairment, while EEG functional connectivity provides complementary information about network organization measured at the time of assessment. Together, these measures characterize different aspects of motor network integrity after stroke.

title: Chronic Exercise Accelerates Disease Progression in a Rat Model of Desminopathy.
journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
abstract: Desminopathy is a progressive myopathy and the most common intermediate filament disease in humans. Desmin is an essential part of the filamentous network that aligns myofibrils, anchors nuclei and mitochondria and connects the z discs to the sarcolemma. We challenged a rat model with a mutation in R349P Des, analogous to the most frequent R350P DES missense mutation in humans, through eccentric-biassed exercise training. R349P Des rats (Des) and their wild type (WT) and heterozygous (HET) littermates were subjected to 4 weeks of downhill running. At the end of 4 weeks, muscles were collected and assessed histologically and biochemically. Des rats demonstrated significantly lower running capacity compared to wild type and heterozygous littermates (p < 0.0001), which exacerbated over the course of the study (p < 0.001). Running performance in Des rats decreased by ~50% after 4 weeks of downhill running. Desmin-positive skeletal muscle aggregates, a histopathological hallmark of desminopathy, were ~2-fold higher after downhill running in the Des group (p < 0.05). On a protein level, we found a differential exercise response of Des compared to WT affecting various cellular pathways concerning autophagy, proteasomal activity, energy metabolism and cytoskeletal proteins. Our results suggest an impaired ability of Des muscle to adapt to chronic eccentric-biassed exercise and a subsequent exacerbation of the functional and histopathological phenotype.

title: Healthcare professionals' perceptions and experiences of promoting physical activity in persons with multiple sclerosis: a systematic review of qualitative evidence.
abstract: To synthesise existing evidence on healthcare professionals' perceptions and experiences of physical activity promotion in persons with multiple sclerosis (MS). The PRISMA and ENTREQ guidelines were used. SCOPUS, CINAHL, PubMed, Embase, PsycINFO and Web of Science databases were searched from database inception to 19 September 2025 to identify eligible studies. Search was limited to peer-reviewed articles, with a focus on healthcare professionals' views about physical activity promotion in persons with MS. Data were extracted and thematically analysed, and identified themes were synthesised. Eight studies met the selection criteria. Identified themes were related to health professional-based factors (knowledge of MS and awareness of physical activity types and benefits, skills, training and education, continuity of support and professional role), organisational factors (coordinated teamwork and proactive approach, policies, protocols and guidelines, availability and accessibility of physical activity opportunities), perceived social factors (social support networks) and perceived patient-related factors (MS-related symptoms, self-efficacy and motivation, limited knowledge and misconceptions, and financial limitations). Findings suggest that improving physical activity promotion in MS care requires MS-specific education and training for healthcare professionals, practical resources such as patient education materials and referral pathways, and stronger cross-sector coordination to sustain consistent practice.

title: Circulating TGF-β1 Increases During Vaginal Progesterone Therapy in Women With a Short Cervix.
abstract: Progesterone is an effective tool for the secondary prevention of spontaneous preterm birth. The aim of this prospective exploratory pilot study was to evaluate the effect of progesterone administration on the number of regulatory T cell (Treg) populations and on the concentrations of the immunoregulatory cytokines IL-10 and TGF-β1 during in vivo progesterone treatment in women at risk of preterm delivery. Pregnant women with a singleton pregnancy (22-30 weeks of gestation) who were at risk of spontaneous preterm delivery and required progesterone therapy were included (n = 21). Peripheral blood was sampled before progesterone administration and twice thereafter during treatment. Seventeen women attended the second visit, while only seven attended the third visit. The control group consisted of prospectively recruited low-risk women (n = 8). Treg numbers were determined by flow cytometry, and plasma concentrations of TGF-β1 and IL-10 were measured by ELISA. In women at risk, plasma TGF-β1 concentrations increased significantly between the first and second sampling (p ≤ 0.01) and remained at a similar level at the third sampling. In contrast, TGF-β1 levels in the control group remained low without statistically significant change. IL-10 concentrations were generally low in both groups. This pilot study was associated with an increase in the immunoregulatory cytokine TGF-β1 following progesterone administration. Although TGF-β1 is produced by several cell types in addition to Tregs, our findings raise the possibility that progesterone reinforces an immunoregulatory pathway relevant to the maintenance of pregnancy in women at risk of preterm birth; however, the present study does not establish this mechanism.

title: Neurofilaments as Biomarkers of Disease Activity and Treatment Response in Spinal Muscular Atrophy.
abstract: Neurofilament light chain (NfL) has been increasingly used in spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) to monitor disease progression and treatment response. We assessed plasma NfL before and after treatment with all three available therapies and in relation to SMA type, age, and functional level. We included all consecutive individuals with SMA who initiated treatment or switched from one treatment to another in whom plasma samples were available at baseline and 12 months post-treatment. Our study included 73 individuals, with Type I (n = 13), II (n = 19), III (n = 33), IV SMA (n = 1) or individuals diagnosed before clinical onset (n = 7); 52/73 were treatment naïve and 21 were included at the time of switching to a new treatment. Mean age at baseline was 17 years, ranging from 0 to 47. At baseline, the NfL levels ranged from 4 to 2682 pg/mL. The overall 12-month changes ranged from -2582.3 to 112 pg/mL. A significant decrease in NfL over time (p < 0.001) was observed. Age was the strongest predictor of the magnitude of NfL reduction. The reduction was greatest in children < 2 years (83%), with progressively smaller reductions in older age groups. SMN2 copy number and SMA type had no significant interactions. Comparison among treatments was challenging because of cohorts' composition; in adults, risdiplam and nusinersen showed similar magnitudes of NfL changes. Our findings expand the literature on NfL in SMA, providing additional data of their changes in response to all three therapies and across a wide spectrum of age and severity.

title: Push-pull hypothesis of Alzheimer's disease.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: The "push-pull" hypothesis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) emerges from a careful examination of the key discoveries over the past 40 years. Specifically, amyloid beta (Aβ) plays a direct role impairing endolysosome activity in neurons and microglia, promoting the collapse of proteostasis, reducing tau degradation, and facilitating the cell-to-cell transmission of aggregated tau. As neurons fail to maintain cell autonomous proteostasis, they transition to actively "pushing" tau pathology into interstitial spaces. This switch represents a rapidly progressing disease state, propagating misfolded tau to synaptically connected neurons. The "pull" hypothesis postulates the spatial distribution of amyloid in cortical regions facilitates the spread of spontaneously aggregating tau from the inferior temporal lobes, manifesting as the symptomology of cognitive decline. In microglia, the Aβ-induced endolysosomal impairment mimics a viral infection, eliciting a chronic and detrimental interferon-type inflammatory response. The push-pull framework makes key predictions about the future success of AD therapeutics.

title: Alterations in the levels of cytokines associated with Th17 cells in the plasma of Guillain-Barre syndrome patients.
journal: JPMA. The Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association
abstract: To compare the cytokines associated with T helper 17 cells between Guillain-Barre syndrome patients and healthy controls. The cross-sectional, comparative study was conducted from March 2024 to February 2025 at the Department of Immunology, University of Health Sciences, Lahore, Pakistan, and comprised Guillain-Barre syndrome patients in group A and healthy controls in group B. Plasma concentrations of interleukin-6 (IL-6), interleukin-17, interleukin-21, interleukin-22 and interleukin-23 in both the groups were quantified using enzymelinked immunosorbent assay. Data was analysed using SPSS 24. Of the 88 subjects, 44(50%) were in group A with mean age 41.6±11.8 years, while 44(50%) were in group B with mean age 39.3±12.4 years. Both the groups had 26(59%) male and 18(41%) female subjects. Serum interleukin-6, interleukin-17 and interleukin-22 levels were significantly higher in group A patients than group B controls (p0.05). Correlation analysis among cytokine levels showed that serum interleukin-21 levels were correlated with interleukin-22 levels in group A patients. Interleukin-17 concentrations did not show any significant relationship with other cytokine levels (p>0.05). Interleukin-6 was negatively correlated with disease duration (p0.05). The activity of T helper 17 cytokines was significantly elevated in Guillain-Barre syndrome patients, underlining the contribution of T helper 17 cell cytokines in Guillain-Barre syndrome and implying that these cytokines can be targeted for therapeutic modulation of the immune response.

title: Validation of the Swedish Lymphedema Functioning, Disability, and Health (Lymph-ICF-UL) Questionnaire: A cross-cultural psychometric study.
journal: Scandinavian journal of surgery : SJS : official organ for the Finnish Surgical Society and the Scandinavian Surgical Society
abstract: The Lymphedema Functioning, Disability, and Health Upper Limb (Lymph-ICF-UL) questionnaire is an internationally recognized instrument for assessing patient-reported functional and activity limitations associated with arm lymphedema following breast cancer surgery. This study aimed to validate the Swedish version of the Lymph-ICF-UL and, additionally, to examine its applicability in an extended cohort without diagnosed arm lymphedema but with potential arm-related impairments following axillary surgery for breast cancer. A cross-cultural psychometric validation was conducted among 27 Swedish-speaking women aged 44-86 years who had undergone node-positive breast cancer surgery 1 year earlier. Data were collected between October 2024 and March 2025. The questionnaire was back-translated into English, revised, and tested for reliability using a test-retest methodology and assessment of internal consistency. Validity was assessed through construct, face, and content validity. Back-translation required minor grammatical adjustments. Test-retest analysis demonstrated good reproducibility, with intraclass correlation coefficients exceeding 0.80 across all domains. Internal consistency was satisfactory, with Cronbach's alpha ranging from 0.76 to 0.96. Construct validity was moderate, with 70.0% of predefined hypotheses for convergent and divergent validity confirmed. Face and content validity analyses led to clarification of the questionnaire instructions. Overall, the items were considered relevant and adequately comprehensive for assessing perceived impairments. The Swedish version of the Lymph-ICF-UL questionnaire is a reliable and valid instrument for assessing arm impairment following axillary surgery for node-positive breast cancer, including among individuals without confirmed arm lymphedema.

title: Scoping review of advance care planning in young and middle-aged adults with a serious illness: Lessons for young-onset dementia.
abstract: Advance care planning (ACP) is widely implemented in older adults with dementia, yet reports focusing on young-onset dementia remain scarce. Valuable insights may be drawn from studies on younger adults with serious chronic illnesses, as they share similar life stages and challenges. To examine ACP in young and middle-aged adults with serious and chronic illnesses and assess their relevance for young-onset dementia. A systematic scoping review. Open Science Framework (https://osf.io/cjwy4). A search was conducted in PubMed, EMBASE, and CINAHL until 19 December 2023. Title/abstract screening was conducted using ASReview. Two authors independently performed the full-text screening and quality assessment. Studies were categorized into 2 groups: (1) process (clinical practice and preferences) and (2) interventions. Fifty-six studies were included, including 26 interventions. Participants preferred initiating ACP either shortly after diagnosis or later, with physicians or general practitioners. In practice, physicians and nurses discussed ACP shortly after diagnosis or later. Preferred topics include end-of-life care and physical, social, psychological, and spiritual/cultural domains. However, in practice, discussions primarily focused on legal representation, end-of-life care, and the physical domain. ACP should adopt a holistic approach at an appropriate stage of the disease trajectory and is a multidisciplinary process. A multidisciplinary team effort could facilitate the integration of the different aspects of ACP. The findings of this review are applicable to young-onset dementia. However, due to the progressive cognitive decline, it should be initiated earlier and revisited throughout the disease trajectory, with increasing family involvement.

title: Predicting adolescent gaming addiction: insights from individual, family, and school-level factors via machine learning.
abstract: Game addiction is increasingly acknowledged as a major adolescent mental health concern worldwide. To better understand its development, it is essential to identify both risk and protective factors. However, most existing studies have focused on only a limited number of variables. To address this gap, this study adopted machine learning to identify the most important predictors across individual, family, and school domains. The analysis was conducted with a sample of 21,239 Chinese parent-adolescent pairs (for parents: 68.92% mothers; Mage = 40.42 years, SD = 5.78 years; for adolescents: 45.00% males; Mage = 13.41 years, SD = 2.14 years). Using the machine learning classification models, this study examined the accuracy of the selected variables in predicting game addiction and explored the relative importance of the studied variables in the prediction process. Both the Random Forest and XGBoost models achieved accuracies exceeding 0.80 and consistently identified several key predictors of game addiction. Risk factors include high levels of externalizing problems and attention problems, being male, bullying victimization, alienation from parents, parental depression, and a performance-oriented school environment. The protective factors include high levels of perseverance, good academic performance, and academic self-efficacy. In conclusion, the findings point out the value of using machine learning approaches to uncover the crucial predictors of game addiction, offering important insights for targeted prevention and intervention efforts across individual, familial, and school contexts.

title: Clinical and functional connectivity changes following left cerebellar continuous theta burst stimulation in schizophrenia with persistent auditory verbal hallucinations: An exploratory open-label study.
abstract: Persistent auditory verbal hallucinations (p-AVH) in schizophrenia are often resistant to treatment and linked to dysconnectivity within the cortical-cerebellar-subcortical network. This study investigated whether continuous theta burst stimulation (cTBS) over the left cerebellum alleviates p-AVH and whether treatment-related functional connectivity (FC) changes predict symptom improvement. Thirty schizophrenia patients with p-AVH received 14-days of left cerebellar cTBS. Whole-brain FC changes (post- vs. pretreatment) were used as neuroimaging features, and the reduction rate of PSYRATS-AH (RR_PSYRATS-AH) at 2 weeks served as the clinical feature. Connectome-based predictive modeling (CPM) was applied, controlling for age, sex, and framewise displacement. cTBS significantly reduced PSYRATS-AH and PANSS P3 scores (all p < 0.05) and improved verbal, attention, and delayed memory performances. CPM revealed that FC changes predicted RR_PSYRATS-AH (r = -0.269, p = 0.047), mainly involving cerebellar-prefrontal, cerebellar-temporal, and cerebellar-subcortical circuits. Left cerebellar cTBS may help alleviate auditory hallucinations and improve cognitive performance in schizophrenia, likely by modulating cortical-cerebellar-subcortical-cortical connectivity, highlighting the cerebellum as a promising target for neuromodulation in treatment-resistant hallucinations.

title: The stroma-vascular compartment: central facilitator of the damage response and repair across organs.
abstract: Tissue injury initiates a complex, multicellular programme whose outcome i.e. functional repair or irreversible fibrosis, is determined by the coordinated activity of the stroma-vascular compartment (SVC). This network of resident fibroblasts, vascular mural cells, endothelial cells and immune populations acts as a gatekeeper of tissue integrity. Following ischaemia, trauma, or mechanical damage, extracellular danger signals are sensed by pattern-recognition receptors and transduced into cell type-specific metabolic and mechanical responses. An initial inflammatory wave clears cellular debris, after which endothelial sprouting and matrix deposition proceed toward scar maturation; a collagen-rich structure whose geometry ultimately governs future perfusion. Epigenetic reprogramming and metabolic rewiring enforce each of these transitions while simultaneously imprinting a memory that skews subsequent responses in the context of ageing, diabetes, chronic inflammation or clonal haematopoiesis. Targeting the SVC, rather than the parenchyma alone, now underpins therapeutic strategies spanning precision senolytics, engineered stromal cell grafts, and biomechanically instructive scaffolds.

title: The Vertebral Nerve as a Selective Target for Upper Limb Sympathetic Blockade: Anatomy, Ultrasound-Guided Technique, and Proof of Concept.
abstract: The vertebral nerve (VN) is a postganglionic sympathetic structure that arises from the cervicothoracic ganglion, ascends alongside the vertebral artery, and provides sympathetic innervation to the upper limb via the brachial plexus. Despite its anatomical relevance, it remains largely unknown to anesthesiologists and pain clinicians. The stellate ganglion block (SGB) is the current standard for upper-limb sympatholysis but produces nonselective effects, including Horner's syndrome and potential cardiac involvement. A more selective approach targeting the VN could achieve equivalent upper-limb sympatholysis while potentially offering a superior safety profile. We conducted a comprehensive anatomical review of the VN, covering its origin, trajectory, branching patterns, and communications with both the cervical spinal nerves and the vertebral plexus. Using this anatomical framework, we describe an ultrasound-guided technique for selective VN blockade at the C7 level, validated with fluoroscopic contrast confirmation. We objectively evaluated clinical efficacy using infrared thermography and laser Doppler flowmetry. The VN is an anatomically consistent and sonographically accessible target for selective upper-limb sympathetic blockade. At this target, effective sympatholysis can be achieved with minimal injectate volumes, thereby avoiding the nonselective effects of conventional SGB. Further studies are needed to compare efficacy, optimal technique parameters, and complication rates with existing approaches.

title: High Prevalence of Childhood Trauma in Australian Adults With Migraine: A Cross-Sectional Study From a Tertiary Headache Center.
abstract: To describe the prevalence of past childhood trauma, including the most common subtypes, in Australian adults with episodic and chronic migraine. Childhood trauma may alter neurobiological processes that lower pain thresholds and amplify pain signals. International studies show that a history of adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) confers double the risk of migraine development in adulthood, compared to those without a history of childhood trauma. The prevalence of childhood trauma in Australian adults with migraine is unknown. Single-center, cross-sectional study of adults with a neurologist-confirmed migraine diagnosis attending a tertiary hospital headache clinic. We invited 1220 eligible patients to complete a validated childhood trauma questionnaire. Responses to the adverse childhood experiences questionnaire, demographic, and clinical data were collected. Significance between binary categorical variables was evaluated using binary logistic regression and reported as odds ratios with 95% confidence intervals. Of the 514 respondents, most were female (82.7%, 425/514) with mean age 47.1 years (standard deviation [SD] 14.0 years). The proportion of those with episodic migraine (274/514, 53.3%) and chronic migraine (240/514, 46.7%) was roughly equal. Most migraine patients reported at least one traumatic childhood event (419/514, 81.5%). Clinically significant past trauma (defined as ACE scores of ≥ 4) was common (198/514, 38.5%). Past verbal abuse was the most common trauma exposure (247/514, 48.1%). Other trauma exposures were psychiatric diagnosis in parent (223/514, 43.4%), emotional neglect (219/514, 42.6%), physical abuse (182/514, 35.4%), sexual abuse (135/514, 26.3%), parental divorce (195/514, 37.9%), parental substance abuse (145/514, 28.2%), witnessing domestic abuse (108/514, 21.0%), physical neglect (64/514, 12.5%), and parental incarceration (28/514, 5.4%). Higher odds of chronic migraine, but not episodic migraine, were observed with past physical abuse (OR 1.56, p = 0.016) and emotional neglect (OR 1.50, p = 0.031); however, significance was lost after Bonferroni correction. Deprivational traumas were associated with higher odds of chronic migraine OR 1.56 (p = 0.013), whereas threat traumas OR 1.41 (p = 0.059) and household dysfunction OR 0.79 (p = 0.217) did not show statistical significance. Australian adults with migraine report high levels of childhood trauma, with verbal abuse being the most common. Understanding the timing, types, severity, and impact of past trauma on the individual may offer further mechanistic insights which could lead to trauma-based therapies for migraine patients.

title: Temporal Stability of Vagally-Mediated Heart Rate Variability Over a One-Year Period: A Latent State-Trait Examination.
abstract: Vagally-mediated heart rate variability (vmHRV) is widely proposed as a biomarker for physical and mental health, but its utility hinges on psychometric robustness, particularly temporal stability and consistency across measurement contexts. Prior reliability studies have been constrained by small samples, short retest intervals, and analytic approaches that cannot disentangle stable individual differences from situational fluctuations and measurement error. The present study examined the temporal and transsituational stability of vmHRV over a 1-year interval in a large, population-based sample (N = 175) from the Dresden Burnout Study. Short-term inter-beat-interval (IBI) recordings were obtained at two annual assessments under two conditions: recumbent recovery following venipuncture and seated rest. Four cardiac and HRV-derived parameters, the established vmHRV indices root mean square of successive differences (RMSSD), percentage of successive RR intervals differing by more than 50 ms (pNN50), and high-frequency power (HF power), complemented by mean RR interval (RR) as a general cardiac timing parameter, were analyzed using single-trait-multistate-method-minus-one [STMSM(M-1)] models within the latent state-trait (LST) framework, with recovery specified as the reference condition and resting modeled as a condition-specific method factor. Reliability ranged from 0.650 to 0.903, and trait specificity ranged from 0.375 to 0.773. RR and RMSSD showed the most consistent trait-like profiles across occasions and conditions. pNN50 showed the highest individual trait-specificity estimate, but also greater heterogeneity across occasions, whereas HF power showed comparatively lower trait specificity and greater occasion-specific variance. Method specificity was small (0.034-0.087), indicating that stable condition-specific deviations from recovery accounted for a limited proportion of variance. These findings support the interpretation of vmHRV, particularly RMSSD and pNN50, as mainly trait-like indicators of cardiac vagal function, while also showing that single short-term assessments contain meaningful occasion-related variance. Standardized assessment conditions and repeated measurements remain essential for biomarker applications of vmHRV.

title: Structural insights into signal transduction in photoactivated adenylyl cyclase through molecular dynamics simulations.
journal: Protein science : a publication of the Protein Society
abstract: OaPAC, from Oscillatoria acuminata, is a homodimer protein consisting of the blue-light using flavin domain and the adenylyl cyclase (AC) domain, linked by long coiled-coil α3-helices. Upon blue-light absorption, a rearrangement of the hydrogen-bonding network involving the flavin chromophore, Y6, and Q48 triggers signal propagation through the α3-helices to the AC domain. While the recent crystallographic structure of the W90-M92-switched conformation in the light state provided significant structural information, the underlying atomistic mechanism of signal transduction remains unclear. In this study, we performed molecular dynamics simulations of OaPAC for four models: wild-type (WT) dark state, W90-M92 unswitched WT light state, W90-M92 switched WT light state, and W90-M92 unswitched L111A/L115A light state. Our results show that the switched WT light-state model exhibits structural fluctuation approximately twice as large as that in the unswitched WT light state. Furthermore, we identified a pronounced transition between two distinct conformational states in the switched WT light-"open" and "closed" -characterized by the angle between the α3-helices and the "handle" region. Notably, the occupancy of the closed conformation was highest in the switched WT light state. In contrast, the non-functional L111A/L115A mutant remained trapped in a rigid open conformation, reflecting its loss of activity and linking structural flexibility to enzymatic competence. These findings suggest that the W90-M92 conformational switch is a critical, multi-step trigger of OaPAC signal transduction, inducing a transient asymmetric (open-closed) conformation and a flexion motion that may facilitate enzymatic activation. This study would provide key atomistic insights for the rational design of advanced optogenetic actuators.

title: A Preliminary Examination of Modulation of the LPP by Personal Preference Rankings for Pleasant Experiences.
abstract: The late positive potential (LPP) is a robust neural marker of attention toward emotionally salient stimuli, yet it is unknown how the LPP is modulated by personal preferences for specific types of pleasant objects/experiences. The present study aimed to evaluate whether personal preferences for pleasant experiences modulate the LPP to images reflecting those situations. Secondary analyses examined whether depressive symptoms and a positive emotion intervention were associated with individual differences in this modulation. College students (N = 92; Mage = 19.44, SD = 1.15) reported depressive symptoms before randomization to a positive emotion intervention (n = 47) or study skills comparison group (n = 45). Participants then rank-ordered a list of eight categories of positive objects/experiences (e.g., cute animals, adventure, social activities, junk food) based on which they enjoyed most and viewed images of each while EEG data were recorded. The LPP was modulated by personal preferences broadly, such that the LPP to images depicting top-ranked pleasant categories was enhanced compared to low-ranked pleasant categories; however, significant effects were not observed linearly between each individual ranking. In secondary analyses, depressive symptoms moderated preference effects on the LPP, with greater symptoms associated with less differentiation between highly preferred and less preferred positive stimuli. The positive emotion intervention did not significantly impact LPP modulation by personal preference. Results highlight the utility of considering personal salience in selecting stimuli for clinical neuroscience tasks and indicate that depression may be characterized by difficulty sustaining attention to personally salient pleasant experiences.

title: Classification of brain variants on fetal ultrasound: international Delphi consensus.
journal: Ultrasound in obstetrics & gynecology : the official journal of the International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology
abstract: To develop an expert consensus classification and management framework for fetal-brain variants identified on prenatal ultrasound across all trimesters of pregnancy that cannot be categorized confidently as either benign or pathological. A two-round international Delphi survey was conducted among experts in fetal medicine and neurosonography, with survey data collected between September 2025 and March 2026. Forty-eight fetal-brain variants, identified through a scoping literature review of PubMed/MEDLINE from database inception to August 2025, performed between June and August 2025, and illustrated with representative ultrasound images, were evaluated. Brain variants were classified according to clinical significance and recommended management into three predefined categories: 'green' (benign variants requiring no additional investigation or follow-up), 'orange' (requiring neurosonographic follow-up) and 'red' (requiring dedicated neurosonography, fetal-brain magnetic resonance imaging and/or genetic investigations). Consensus was predefined as ≥ 70% agreement. In Round 2, experts confirmed their agreement regarding categorization of variants that had reached consensus in Round 1 and reassessed variants that did not reach initial consensus. Forty-eight experts from 14 countries participated in Round 1 and 39 (81.3%) completed both rounds. Of the 48 evaluated variants, 35 (72.9%) reached consensus after two rounds: 12 were classified as 'green', seven as 'orange' and 16 as 'red'. Green variants included isolated choroid plexus cysts < 10 mm across all trimesters, regular asymmetry of the choroid plexuses, isolated cavum septations, cavum vergae, cavum velum interpositum, isolated small cavum septi pellucidi with intact corpus callosum and dolichocephaly with normal head circumference and normal brain morphology. Orange variants included isolated enlargement of intracranial translucency with preserved anatomy, large or bilateral choroid plexus cysts, isolated enlargement of subarachnoid spaces without compression and isolated cyst of the cavum septi pellucidi. Red variants included abnormal posterior fossa markers (loss of normal three-space anatomy, increased brainstem-vermis angle, reduced brainstem-occipital bone distance), periventricular cysts associated with adjacent white-matter abnormalities, thickened corpus callosum and distortion of the interhemispheric fissure, among other findings. Thirteen (27.1%) variants failed to reach consensus, highlighting persistent uncertainty in interpreting subtle isolated asymmetries and selected cystic variants. This international Delphi consensus proposes an initial expert-derived classification of commonly encountered feta-brain variants on ultrasound. Because the classification has not been validated against postnatal imaging or neurodevelopmental outcomes and reproducibility has not been assessed, prospective evaluation is required before it can be applied in routine practice. © 2026 International Society of Ultrasound in Obstetrics and Gynecology.

title: Optimized amyloid-β PET centiloid and cognitive cutoffs predict progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer's dementia.
journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
abstract: This study aimed to develop optimized prognostic cutoffs for amyloid-β-positron emission tomography (Aβ-PET) and Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) that predict 3-year progression from Clinical Dementia Rating Global (CDR-Global) score 0.5 to 1.0 in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) participants and validate against cognitive decline/functional trajectories. We analyzed 454 CDR-global = 0.5 Aβ-positive (> 25 Centiloid [CL]) MCI participants from Australian Imaging Biomarkers and Lifestyle (AIBL) (N = 99) and Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative (ADNI) (N = 355), followed up to seven years. Youden index derived optimal Aβ-PET and MMSE thresholds for 3-year progression. Participants were stratified into four groups by combined Aβ-PET/MMSE status. Adjusted Cox models (age, sex, education, apolipoprotein E [APOE] ε4) assessed progression to CDR-Global score of 1.0 Alzheimer's disease (AD) dementia (confirmed with Aβ-PET); adjusted linear mixed models assessed CDR Sum of Boxes (CDR-SoB) and Preclinical Alzheimer's Cognitive Composite (PACC) trajectories. Optimal cutoffs were Aβ-PET > 71 CL (hazard ratio [HR] = 2.67; 3-year risk = 36.7%) and MMSE score of < 27 (HR = 2.27; 36.8%). The combined high Aβ/low MMSE group showed a 6.39-fold risk and 47.8% 3-year progression, with the steepest decline. Prognostically optimized Aβ-PET and MMSE cutoffs improve 3-year risk stratification beyond common diagnostic thresholds, supporting dual-cutoff prognostic enrichment.

title: In Memoriam Paul Witkovsky (1937-2026) - True Tenure at Last.
Refining the Overlap Between Burning Mouth Syndrome and Occlusal Dysesthesia (Phantom Bite Syndrome): Evidence From Clinical and Cerebral Perfusion Studies.
abstract: Burning mouth syndrome (BMS) and occlusal dysesthesia/phantom bite syndrome (OD/PBS) are clinically distinct but can overlap. BMS is characterised mainly by burning oral pain, whereas OD/PBS is characterised by a persistent uncomfortable bite perception. These different symptom modalities should not be taken as proof of completely separate mechanisms, nor should clinical co-occurrence be taken as proof of identical pathology. The revised framework highlights a partly shared trigeminal somatosensory substrate together with condition-specific sensory processing. Eating-related symptoms and functional performance may dissociate, so both should be assessed separately. The clinical implication is to phenotype overlap carefully and avoid repeated irreversible occlusal interventions for complaints without objective structural explanation.

title: Comparing the analgesic effect of fluoxetine plus vitamin e with vitamin e alone on mastodynia due to fibrocystic breast disease: a randomized double-blind clinical trial.
abstract: Mastodynia is a common symptom in women with fibrocystic breast disease and can substantially impair quality of life. Although vitamin E is frequently used for symptom relief, the potential additional analgesic effect of fluoxetine remains unclear. This study aimed to compare the analgesic effect of fluoxetine plus vitamin E with that of vitamin E plus placebo in women with mastodynia associated with fibrocystic breast disease. This double-blind, randomized clinical trial enrolled 78 women with mastodynia associated with fibrocystic breast disease who attended clinics affiliated with Shahrekord University of Medical Sciences, Shahrekord, Iran. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) to receive either vitamin E (400 IU/day) plus fluoxetine (10 mg/day) or vitamin E (400 IU/day) plus placebo for 8 weeks. Randomization was computer-generated, allocation was concealed using identical medication packaging, and participants, investigators, and outcome assessors were blinded to treatment allocation. The primary outcome was breast pain intensity, assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) at baseline and at 1 and 2 months after treatment initiation. Secondary outcomes included breast heaviness, breast itching, and adverse events. Data were analyzed using repeated-measures analysis of variance and appropriate categorical tests. Seventy participants (35 per group) completed the study and were included in the analysis. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were comparable between the two groups. Repeated-measures analysis of variance demonstrated significant effects of treatment group (F (1,68) = 11.056, P = 0.001), time (F (2,136) = 164.321, P < 0.001), and the group-by-time interaction (F (2,136) = 60.996, P < 0.001) on breast pain intensity. No significant between-group differences were observed at baseline or after 1 month of treatment; however, after 2 months, breast pain intensity was significantly lower in the fluoxetine plus vitamin E group than in the vitamin E plus placebo group (P < 0.001). Breast heaviness was also significantly less frequent in the combination therapy group after 1 month (P = 0.009). Three participants in the fluoxetine group discontinued treatment because of adverse events, and no serious adverse events were reported in either group. The addition of fluoxetine to vitamin E improved breast pain after 8 weeks compared with vitamin E plus placebo in women with mastodynia associated with fibrocystic breast disease. These findings suggest that fluoxetine may be a useful adjunctive treatment; however, larger multicenter randomized trials with longer follow-up are needed to confirm its efficacy and safety. Iranian Registry of Clinical Trials (IRCT20200205046381N1), registered on February 28, 2020.

title: Spatial transcriptomics and dual tracer mapping reveal Wnt-driven attenuation of blood-brain barrier permeability Induced by endothelial EphA4 deficiency.
abstract: Blood-brain barrier (BBB) disruption is a key pathological event following traumatic brain injury (TBI), yet its molecular and spatial characteristics remain incompletely understood. Here, we developed a dual-tracer mapping system to assess the temporal and spatial dynamics of BBB permeability following controlled cortical impact (CCI) injury in EphA4f/f VE-Cadherin-CreERT2 (KO) and EphA4f/f (WT) mice. By tracking Evans Blue Dye (EBD), sodium fluorescein (NaFl), and endogenous IgG deposition, we identified distinct patterns of vascular tracer extravasation in the injured cortex and hippocampus. NaFl, a small-molecule tracer, continued to extravasate for 7 days post-injury, whereas EBD leakage diminished after 4 days. Notably, endothelial EphA4 deletion significantly reduced size-dependent vascular tracer extravasation. To further investigate molecular pathways associated with altered BBB permeability, we integrated spatial transcriptomics with tracer quantification, revealing that endothelial EphA4 ablation upregulates BBB-associated genes (Tjp2, Tjp3, Cldn1, and Ocln) and injury-responsive genes linked to injury-responsive genes (Nr4a1 and Npas4). Wnt signaling genes were similarly upregulated in the KO cortex, and pharmacological inhibition of Frizzled-4 (FZD4)/Wnt signaling attenuated the reduction in vascular tracer extravasation observed in KO mice. Conversely, pharmacological activation of Wnt signaling with the FZD4 agonist FZM1.8 in WT mice reduced lesion volume and vascular tracer extravasation. Overall, these findings demonstrate the utility of combining spatial transcriptomics with dual-tracer mapping to identify region-specific transcriptional programs associated with BBB permeability following CCI injury and to define the contribution of EphA4/Wnt signaling to vascular responses after TBI. Together, these findings identify Wnt signaling as a promising therapeutic pathway for reducing vascular permeability and limiting secondary brain injury following TBI.

title: Neuroepigenetic programming by the maternal environment. Part B: independent contribution of methylation and hydroxymethylation in the offspring's olfactory bulb following preconceptional weight loss in mice.
abstract: Recent studies indicate that inadequate maternal diet can influence offspring physiology, metabolism and cognitive health, but the impact of the preconception period remains largely unexplored. We previously showed that maternal weight loss prior to conception affects metabolic outcomes and olfactory-driven behaviors in mouse offspring. To explore whether these intergenerational effects are linked to epigenetic mechanisms in the olfactory bulb (OB), we investigated changes in DNA methylation, specifically 5-methylcytosine (5mC) and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC), the latter being relatively abundant in the brain but still poorly characterized. We profiled DNA methylation and hydroxymethylation using Reduced Representation Bisulfite Sequencing (RRBS) and oxidative RRBS (oxRRBS) on OBs from offspring born to control or weight loss mothers, to enable a distinct quantification of 5mC and 5hmC levels at the same CpG sites. While 5mC was globally more abundant in the OB, a subset of CpGs showed high 5hmC levels that varied with maternal condition. Differential analysis identified more differential hydroxymethylated CpG (DhMCs, n = 2631) than differential methylated positions (DMC, n = 1834), indicating a stronger impact of maternal WL on hydroxymethylation. Both DMCs and DhMCs were enriched in genes involved in synaptic function, neuronal signaling, and energy metabolism. However, uniquely modified CpGs, i.e. those detected as modified in only one assay (RRBS or oxRRBS), revealed distinct functional profiles: uniquely differentially hydroxymethylated CpGs (uniqDhMCs) were enriched in genes related to neuronal activity and plasticity, while uniquely differentially methylated CpGs (uniqDMCs) were associated with chromatin remodeling and transcriptional regulation. These findings suggest that, although 5mC and 5hmC can impact similar pathways, they contribute differently to gene regulation in response to early-life nutritional environments. Our study highlights the feasibility of integrating 5mC and 5hmC analyses and uncovers their distinct genomic distributions. The maternal preconceptional weight loss induces lasting and specific epigenetic changes in the OB, notably through 5hmC-specific targeting on genes involved in neuronal activity. By distinguishing between shared and unique DMCs and DhMCs, we reveal complementary and functionally distinct contributions of 5mC and 5hmC to brain plasticity. These findings underscore the importance of integrating both epigenetic marks to fully understand how early-life environmental cues shape neural function and behavior.
keywords: Developmental Origins of Health and Disease

title: Effects of sportsmetrics training on biomechanical and functional performance outcomes related to ACL injury risk: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: This meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of SportsMetrics training (SMT) on ACL injury-related biomechanical deficits and functional performance outcomes in athletes. Literature searches were conducted in four databases from inception to May 10, 2026. The RoB 2 and ROBINS-I tools were used to assess the risk of bias, while meta-analyses and sensitivity analyses were performed using CMA 4 software. The GRADE approach was applied to evaluate the quality of evidence. Primary outcomes were dynamic knee valgus (DKV) and the Landing Error Scoring System (LESS). Secondary outcomes included core strength, agility, dynamic balance, speed, and power. Nine studies (310 athletes, predominantly female) were included. SMT was associated with changes in surrogate biomechanical outcomes, including DKV (SMD: -1.09, p < 0.0001) and LESS (SMD: -1.08, p < 0.0001), as well as functional performance outcomes: agility, dynamic balance, power, and speed. Core strength (SMD: 0.57, p = 0.154) showed non-significant changes. SMT was associated with improvements in several biomechanical and functional outcomes. Higher-quality RCTs and prospective injury registration outcomes are required to confirm these findings. However, the relationship between improvements in these surrogate outcomes and actual ACL injury reduction remains unestablished. This study was a priori registered at PROSPERO (CRD420261389110).

title: METTL3-mediated m6A modification of circNOTCH2 attenuates osteogenic impairment of PDLSCs in inflammatory microenvironment via the MiR-193b-3p/KCNJ2/NLRP3 axis.
abstract: Persistent inflammation associated with periodontitis significantly impairs the osteogenic differentiation potential of periodontal ligament stem cells (PDLSCs). Therefore, maintaining the osteogenic capacity of PDLSCs under inflammatory conditions represents a key therapy target for reducing periodontal bone loss. This study aims to investigate the mechanism by which the m6A-modified circular RNA hsa_circ_0005737 (circNOTCH2) regulates osteogenic differentiation of PDLSCs in the inflammatory microenvironment. CircRNAs were screened via bioinformatics analysis. Plasmid overexpression and siRNA knockdown were employed to modulate gene expression. The regulatory role of circNOTCH2 in inflammatory PDLSCs and periodontitis was assessed through transcriptomic sequencing, Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) staining, Alizarin Red S (ARS) staining, and a murine model of periodontitis. The N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation modification of circNOTCH2 was validated by methylated RNA immunoprecipitation (MeRIP). The underlying molecular mechanisms of circNOTCH2 were investigated using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), immunofluorescence (IF) staining, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and Western blot analysis. Under inflammatory conditions, the expression of circNOTCH2 is significantly upregulated. Transcriptomic sequencing analysis revealed that circNOTCH2 is primarily associated with osteogenic differentiation of stem cells and the NLRP3 inflammasome pathway. Interestingly, overexpression of circNOTCH2 promotes osteogenic differentiation in PDLSCs. Further investigation demonstrates that this pro-osteogenic effect is mediated through a compensatory upregulation of circNOTCH2. CircNOTCH2 acts as a molecular sponge for miR-193b-3p, leading to the upregulation of KCNJ2 expression. This subsequently inhibits NLRP3 inflammasome activation and counteracts the suppressive effects of inflammation on the osteogenic potential of PDLSCs. Furthermore, the study revealed that METTL3-mediated m6A modification enhances the stability of circNOTCH2. As an upstream regulatory molecule, METTL3 positively influences the regulatory role of circNOTCH2 on PDLSCs. In summary, our findings demonstrated that m6A-modified circNOTCH2 is compensatorily up-regulated in inflammatory PDLSCs and alleviates inflammation-induced impairment of osteogenic differentiation via the miR-193b-3p/KCNJ2/NLRP3 axis. These findings suggest that circNOTCH2 may represent a significant molecular target for the treatment of periodontitis.

title: Correction: Explaining the association between social and lifestyle factors and cognitive functions: a pathway analysis in the Memento cohort.
Domiciliary fractional exhaled nitric oxide predicts exacerbation risk and guides ICS tapering in controlled asthma.
abstract: Fluctuating airway inflammation drives asthma clinical variability, yet current monitoring lacks dynamic assessment. Domiciliary fractional exhaled nitric oxide (FeNO) measurements offer real-time inflammatory tracking. To explore asthma clinical phenotypes and prognosis using FeNO trajectories. In this 24-week prospective cohort study, 89 participants recorded daily FeNO and completed weekly online questionnaires. ICS dose adjustments, including step down decisions, followed GINA stepwise approach based on clinical stability. Spirometry, blood eosinophil counts, exacerbation rates, and corticosteroid requirements were assessed at baseline and during stable-phase control. Patients were classified into three phenotypes based on baseline and stable‑phase FeNO using the 50 ppb threshold (ATS guideline) and a ≥ 20% reduction criterion. Clustering analysis validated the classification. Three phenotypes were identified: (1) Low Group (n = 34): Sustained FeNO 78 ppb combined with FEV₁/FVC > 75% predicted the High phenotype (AUC 0.89, 95% CI 0.79-0.98). Home‑based FeNO monitoring identifies three clinically distinct asthma phenotypes with different treatment responses and ICS tapering safety. The 41‑day stabilization window and prediction model provide an evidence‑based framework for personalized, biomarker‑guided asthma management.

title: Are oral hygiene behaviors associated with lower stroke risk? A systematic review.
abstract: This study aims to systematically synthesize observational evidence on the association between oral hygiene behaviors, including tooth brushing, interdental cleaning, dental visits, and professional dental cleaning, and stroke risk in adults. A PRISMA-compliant systematic review was conducted by searching PubMed, Scopus, Embase and google scholar on November 26, 2025. Observational studies evaluating oral hygiene behaviors in relation to stroke or cerebrovascular outcomes were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle Ottawa Scale (NOS). Due to substantial heterogeneity in exposures, outcomes, and effect measures, findings were synthesized narratively. Thirteen studies (9 cohort, 4 cross-sectional) involving over 1.1 million participants were included. Eleven studies evaluated tooth brushing; six out of eight cohort studies and one of three cross sectional ones reported significant inverse associations. Interdental cleaning generally demonstrated a protective directional association with stroke risk; however, several studies reported non-significant associations following multivariable adjustment. Regular dental visits and professional dental cleaning were associated with reductions in stroke risk across cohort studies. Cross-sectional evidence for brushing alone and dental visit frequency was less consistent. Observational evidence supports an association between favorable oral hygiene behaviors, particularly frequent tooth brushing and professional dental cleaning, and reduced stroke risk. Oral hygiene may represent an underrecognized component of vascular prevention strategies.

title: Characteristics associated with efficacy of hypoxia-inducible factor-prolyl hydroxylase inhibitors in renal anemia patients: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Hypoxia-inducible factor-prolyl hydroxylase inhibitors (HIF-PHIs) are novel drugs used to treat renal anemia patients.However, their efficacy in elevating hemoglobin levels varies among patients. We aimed to identify characteristics that could influence hemoglobin level in renal anemia patients treated with HIF-PHIs. We conducted a retrospective cohort study in renal anemia patients treated with HIF-PHIs (roxadustat and enarodustat) with CKD stages 3-5 from 2023 to 2025, and both non-dialysis patients and dialysis patients were included. Patients with CKD stage 5 requiring dialysis were classified as having end-stage kidney disease (ESKD), these patients were also included. Patients were assigned into Hb responder or non-responder group based on hemoglobin changes (elevation, non-elevation) from 0 to 3 months. Logistic regression was applied to explore characteristics associated with the effect of HIF-PHI on achieving targeted hemoglobin levels in renal anemia patients. A total of 459 renal anemia patients were included, including 341 and 118 in the Hb responder and non-responder groups, respectively. There were significant differences in lymphocyte percentage, neutrophil percentage, phosphorus, chloride, blood urea nitrogen, and serum creatinine between the Hb responder and non-responder groups (P < 0.05). A higher probability of Hb response to HIF-PHI therapy was observed when hemoglobin levels were between 100 and 110 g/L. Treatment response was superior when HIF-PHIs were initiated prior to chronic kidney disease stage 4. Logistic regression analysis identified initial hemoglobin levels of 80-90 g/L as an independent risk factor affecting HIF-PHI efficacy, with satisfactory model performance. Renal function stage and electrolyte disturbances were associated with Hb response to HIF-PHIs in patients with renal anemia. Early and appropriate treatment timing may enhance the efficacy of HIF-PHIs to elevate hemoglobin levels in these patients.

title: A glutamatergic circuit from the piriform cortex to the mediodorsal thalamus regulates trigeminal neuropathic pain and comorbid cognitive impairment in mice.
journal: The journal of headache and pain
abstract: Trigeminal neuropathic pain (TNP) is a chronic, debilitating pain disorder affecting the orofacial region. Patients often experience concomitant cognitive impairment, severely impacting their quality of life. The principal neural circuit mechanisms that link TNP to cognitive dysfunction remain unclear. The piriform cortex (PIR), primarily recognised for its role in olfaction, has not been systematically investigated in trigeminal neuropathic pain processing or pain-related cognitive dysfunction. This study utilised pseudorabies virus-mediated multisynaptic retrograde tracing to map whole-brain anatomical connectivity associated with orofacial sensory pathways. c-Fos immunofluorescence staining and in vivo fibre-optic calcium signalling recordings were used to detect alterations in glutamatergic neuronal activity within the PIR of TNP model mice. Chemogenetic and optogenetic techniques were employed to manipulate PIR glutamatergic (PIRGlu) neurons in a bidirectional manner, validating their functional roles in pain and cognitive regulation. Anterograde viral tracing was integrated with circuit-specific chemogenetic intervention to elucidate downstream regulatory pathways. This study identified the PIR as a previously unrecognized brain region anatomically associated with trigeminal neuropathic pain-related pathways, providing evidence for its potential involvement in TNP. PIRGlu neurons in TNP model mice exhibited marked burst-like activation, with in vivo calcium activity intensity exhibiting considerable synchronisation with facial pain-sensitive behaviour. Chemogenetic inhibition of PIRGlu neurons significantly increased pain thresholds and ameliorated cognitive deficits in TNP mice, whereas selective activation of PIRGlu neurons in sham mice recapitulated the pain-cognition comorbidity phenotype, demonstrating the essential role of these neurons in mediating pain-related cognitive dysfunction. Viral tracing identified the mediodorsal thalamus (MD) as a critical downstream target of PIRGlu neurons. Electrophysiological recordings further confirmed that PIRGlu neurons establish direct excitatory monosynaptic connections with MD neurons, with fast glutamatergic transmission predominantly mediated by AMPA receptor-dependent signalling. Specific disruption of the PIRGlu-MD circuit simultaneously alleviated pain and cognitive impairment in model mice, while inhibition of PIRGlu neurons markedly reduced calcium activity in downstream MD neurons. This study highlights the PIRGlu-MD circuit as an important pathway contributing to TNP-cognitive impairment comorbidity. Furthermore, it augments our understanding of the non-olfactory physiological functions of the PIR, offering a novel potential target for investigating the mechanisms underlying the association of chronic pain with cognitive impairment.

title: VAMP2-mediated PPAR signaling modulates mitophagy and inflammatory responses in Mg2+-free induced HT22 neuronal cells.
abstract: To explore the neuroprotective effects and molecular mechanism of the VAMP2-mediated PPAR signaling pathway on neuronal mitophagy using an in vitro seizure-like injury model. A seizure model was established by culturing mouse hippocampal HT22 cells in Mg2+-free medium. siRNA-mediated gene knockdown and lentiviral overexpression were applied to regulate VAMP2 expression. Bioinformatic analysis via GeneCards and STRING was performed to predict the interaction between VAMP2 and the PPAR pathway. Cell phenotypes and molecular alterations were detected by RT-qPCR, Western blotting, flow cytometry, ELISA and immunofluorescence. The PPAR inhibitor GW9662 was used to verify the regulatory relationship between VAMP2 and PPAR signaling. VAMP2 expression was significantly downregulated in Mg2+-free solution -treated neurons. VAMP2 overexpression increased cell viability, inhibited apoptosis and restored mitochondrial membrane potential (p<0.001). VAMP2 upregulated mitophagy-related proteins (LC3-II/I, PINK1, and Parkin), reduced ROS and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, TNF-α), and balanced the expression of synaptic proteins NMDAR1 and GABAA1. Bioinformatic and experimental results demonstrated that VAMP2 acts as an upstream regulator to promote the expression and nuclear translocation of PPARα/γ. Blocking PPAR signaling with GW9662 completely abolished the protective effects of VAMP2, leading to impaired mitophagy, mitochondrial dysfunction and synaptic imbalance. A novel VAMP2-PPAR-mitophagy axis was identified in seizure-injured neurons, which maintains mitochondrial integrity and alleviates neuronal damage. Targeting the crosstalk between vesicle trafficking and nuclear receptor signaling may provide potential therapeutic ideas for hyperexcitability-related neurodegenerative disorders. Not applicable.

title: Early Responses to Nonconscious Fear-Conditioned Faces-An ERP Study.
abstract: Prioritized processing of emotionally relevant faces compared to neutral faces is reflected in differential event-related potentials (ERPs). However, there is an ongoing debate about the extent to which faces, in general, and fear-conditioned faces, in particular, enhance early ERPs when they are not consciously perceived. Here, we tested whether early ERP components (P1 and N170) differentiate between fear-conditioned (CS+) and non-aversive (CS-) faces presented for 17 ms in a backward-masking design using a sequential Bayesian sampling procedure (N = 40). Consciousness was manipulated by presenting the mask directly (0 ms) or after a delay (200 ms) following the target stimulus. Participants were asked to rate their subjective perception after each trial to differentiate between trials in which they perceived nothing beyond the mask, brief glimpses of anything other than a face, vague impressions of a face, or clear impressions of a face. CS+ as compared to CS- faces led to increased N170 amplitudes in the conscious condition among successfully conditioned participants, but not in the nonconscious condition, while no differential effects were observed for the other ERP components. Thus, the data do not support the assumption that fear-conditioned stimuli are processed nonconsciously in the visual cortex.

title: Converging pathomechanisms link SARS-CoV-2 infection with major neurodegenerative diseases.
abstract: Neurological complications are among typical clinical manifestations, both during the acute phase of SARS-CoV-2 infection and long-term post-acute COVID-19 sequelae, i.e., Long COVID. A growing body of evidence connects SARS-CoV-2 infection to systemic inflammation, peripheral immune dysregulation, functional alteration of the blood-brain barrier (BBB), neuroinflammatory processes, mitochondrial dysfunction and pathological protein aggregation, all of which are central to the pathogenesis of major neurodegenerative diseases. In this review, we discuss the converging shared underlying molecular mechanisms that link the 'acute' SARS-CoV-2 infection that often only lasts for days and 'chronic' neurodegenerative diseases that often take decades to develop. We further review human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs)-derived brain organoid and BBB models for Parkinson's disease (PD) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) as well as artificial intelligence (AI)-facilitated knowledge graph methods that are used to hypothesize and validate the potential mechanistic links. We propose that besides the established links between viral infections and neurodegenerative or neuroinflammatory conditions, such as Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) in multiple sclerosis or herpes zoster in AD, SARS-CoV-2 infection might be another important factor driving the future burden of the most common neurodegenerative diseases.

title: Role of Arachidonic Acid Metabolic Dysregulation in Sheep Brain Injury Caused by Coenurus cerebralis Infection.
abstract: Coenurus cerebralis (C. cerebralis) infection is a common parasitic disease in sheep that causes severe neurological damage. However, the underlying metabolic changes triggered by this pathogen in host sheep remain poorly understood. This study aimed to explore the effects of C. cerebralis infection on in vivo metabolic functions in sheep. Broad-targeted blood metabolomics was used to screen differential serum metabolites between C. cerebralis-infected sheep (BE-P group) and healthy sheep (BE-N group). Combined with KEGG enrichment analysis and ELISA assays, we further validated key metabolic molecules and related pathways. A total of 25 significantly differential metabolites were identified, including 19 upregulated and 6 downregulated metabolites. KEGG enrichment indicated that the arachidonic acid (AA) metabolic pathway was the most significantly dysregulated pathway. ELISA results showed that serum phospholipids (PLs), phospholipase A2 (PLA2), AA, prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), thromboxane B2 (TXB2), 5-hydroxyeicosatetraenoic acid (5-HETE), leukotriene B4 (LTB4), cysteinyl leukotriene receptor 2 (CysLT2R), and soluble epoxide hydrolase (sEH) were markedly increased, whereas epoxy-eicosatrienoic acids (EETs) were decreased in the BE-P group. C. cerebralis infection disturbed the AA metabolic pathway, with abnormal activation of its downstream cyclooxygenase (COX), lipoxygenase (LOX), and cytochrome P450 (CYP450) branches. These changes were accompanied by neuroinflammation, oxidative stress and microcirculation disturbance, which ultimately disrupted cerebral metabolism. Notably, serum CysLT2R level in the BE-P group was 2.13-fold higher than that in the BE-N group, representing the most prominent difference. CysLT2R may mediate neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption and neuronal injury through the Gαq signaling pathway. C. cerebralis infection disturbs the arachidonic acid metabolic pathway and activates its downstream metabolic cascades. CysLT2R is a key altered molecule, which may participate in the brain injury induced by C. cerebralis infection.

title: Reliability shapes coordinate frame selection in spatial working memory.
abstract: The format of spatial representation is a fundamental issue in cognitive research. Previous studies have shown that blank and grid environments selectively induce polar and Cartesian coordinate patterns, respectively. However, these findings are largely based on reliable blocked designs, leaving it unclear whether such representational formats remain stable under environmental uncertainty. Using a spatial location reproduction paradigm, we applied error correlation analysis to infer the underlying coordinate signatures, while introducing contextual reliability (grid/blank) during either the response phase (Experiment 1) or the encoding phase (Experiment 2). In Experiment 1, when uncertainty was introduced at retrieval, polar-consistent error patterns remained relatively preserved under blank encoding. Experiment 2 revealed that encoding-phase uncertainty significantly reduced the difference between polar and Cartesian error patterns across conditions. Meanwhile, encoding-phase uncertainty led to a preferential reliance on Cartesian coordinate features. Within the error-correlation framework, these findings delineate what contextual uncertainty changes (Cartesian signature expression; frame selection) and what it leaves unchanged (a robust polar signature under encoding reliability).
