OPEN PRACTICES STATEMENT: The data and analysis code for both experiments are publicly available at the Open Science Framework ( https://osf.io/znrb6/ ). Neither experiment was preregistered.

title: When is stem cell-related research ethical? : An Ethics Framework for Basic Stem Cell-Related Research.
Deep learning-based segmentation of the ischemic core and severe hypodensity on noncontrast head CT compared with CT perfusion and diffusion-weighted imaging.
abstract: To compare the spatial overlap, imaging marker agreement, and outcome associations of acute ischemic regions of interest (ROIs) using deep-learning NCCT (DLNCCT) versus manual NCCT, CTP, and DWI-based segmentations. We trained a deep learning model to segment ischemic ROIs on admission NCCT (DLNCCT). DLNCCT was compared with manual NCCT, CTP (rCBF < 30%/38%), and DWI using the Dice similarity coefficient (mean ± SD), Bland-Altman analysis (mean difference [95% CI]), and concordance correlation coefficient (CCC). For each ROI, we compared NCCT imaging biomarkers: average lesion density (HU); modified net water uptake (mNWU in %); total volume (mL); and hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volume (mL). DLNCCT biomarkers were associated with reversed 90-day ordinal modified Rankin Scale (genOR [95% CI]). We used 218/762 train/test cases. Dice was 0.30 ± 0.30 between DLNCCT and manual segmentation, 0.22 ± 0.25 between DLNCCT-DWI, and 0.15 ± 0.22/0.21 ± 0.24 between CTP (rCBF < 30%/< 38%)-DWI. DLNCCT-DWI biomarker agreement was -1 HU (95% CI: -7; 6) for average density (CCC: 0.71), 4.9% (95% CI: -7.0; 16.8) for mNWU (CCC: 0.35), -16 mL (95% CI: -108; 76) for total volume (CCC: 0.57), and -4 mL (95% CI: -31; 23) for hypodense lesion volume (CCC: 0.75). Average lesion density (1.11 [95% CI: 1.06; 1.16]) and hypodense volume (0.85 [95% CI: 0.72; 0.99]) were associated with 90-day mRS. Spatial and biomarker agreement between DLNCCT and DWI was suboptimal but comparable to CTP-DWI. Nevertheless, DLNCCT-derived average lesion density and hypodense volume were associated with functional outcomes. Question Deep-learning models segment ischemic tissue on NCCT, but their spatial overlap and accuracy of imaging biomarker assessment relative to DWI and CTP core remain unclear. Findings Deep-learning NCCT segmentation showed good agreement with DWI in measuring hypodense (≤ 26 HU) volumes (- 4 mL [95% CI: -31; 23]; CCC 0.75). Clinical relevance Despite limited spatial overlap, NCCT-derived deep learning biomarkers showed agreement comparable to DWI, with improved performance in patients with poor ASPECTS and collateral scores. Hypodense volume and average lesion density were associated with functional outcome.

title: The positive allosteric modulator of the GABAB receptor, ASP8062, attenuates alcohol self-administration in female Sardinian alcohol-preferring rats.
abstract: Four-day intragastric treatment with the positive allosteric modulator of the GABAB receptor, ASP8062 (1, 3, and 10 mg/kg), suppressed operant oral alcohol self-administration in male and female Sprague Dawley (SD) rats (Haile et al., Psychopharmacology 238:2587-2600, 2021). Conversely, in a double-blind placebo-controlled trial, 6-week treatment with ASP8062 (25 mg/day, corresponding to the 3-mg/kg rat dose) failed to attenuate alcohol craving and consumption in individuals with moderate or severe alcohol use disorder (AUD) (Schacht et al., Alcohol Clin Exp Res 48:2352-2363, 2024). Reverse-translational dose-ranging studies in animal models of AUD were suggested. In keeping with this purpose, the present study tested ASP8062 on operant oral alcohol self-administration in selectively bred Sardinian alcohol-preferring (sP) rats, a validated animal model of AUD. Female sP rats were trained to lever-respond for alcohol under the fixed ratio 5 schedule of reinforcement. Once lever-responding for alcohol was high and steady, rats underwent a 4-day intragastric treatment with ASP8062 (3, 10, and 17 mg/kg). Only the 17-mg/kg dose reduced, by approximately 40%, lever-responding for alcohol and estimated amount of self-administered alcohol. No dose of ASP8062 altered motor-coordination, as indicated by the results of a concurrent inverted-screen test. ASP8062 in sP rats was remarkably less potent compared to previous observations in SD rats, suggesting that higher doses of ASP8062 may be needed in rats modeling AUD. If ideally transposed to humans, these data suggest that future clinical studies should consider testing higher doses of ASP8062 before reaching definitive conclusions on its therapeutic potential.

title: Effects of Pantoprazole on PTZ-Kindling Progression and Associated Neuroinflammatory and Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress Responses in Rats.
abstract: Epileptogenesis is characterized by complex molecular changes, including neuroinflammation, endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress, and apoptosis, contributing to seizures and associated cognitive and behavioral impairments. Pantoprazole, a proton pump inhibitor, has demonstrated anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective properties. This study investigated its effects on PTZ-kindling progression and associated molecular alterations in a pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced rat model. Adult male Wistar albino rats (n = 30) were subjected to chronic PTZ kindling (30 mg/kg, i.p., on alternate day, 15 injections). Pantoprazole (5 and 10 mg/kg) or valproic acid (150 mg/kg) was administered prior to PTZ. Seizure severity was scored using the Racine scale. Cognitive and anxiety-like behaviors were assessed by passive avoidance and open field tests. Neuroinflammatory (TNF-α, NF-κB, IL-1β, COX-1/2), ER stress (GRP78, ATF4, CHOP), and apoptotic (caspase-3/9) markers were measured by ELISA in cortex and hippocampus. NF-κB, iNOS, and p-NMDAR2B expression in hippocampal CA1 and CA3 regions were evaluated immunohistochemically. Histopathological analysis was also performed. PTZ significantly increased seizure severity, memory impairment, and anxiety-like behavior, alongside elevated neuroinflammatory, ER stress, and apoptotic markers. Increased NF-κB, iNOS, and p-NMDAR2B expression and neuronal degeneration were observed in hippocampal regions. Pantoprazole dose-dependently attenuated PTZ-kindling progression, improved behavioral outcomes, and reduced the measured molecular alterations. Histopathological and immunohistochemical findings confirmed decreased neuronal damage and marker expression. Pantoprazole demonstrated protective effects in the PTZ-kindling model, which may be associated with modulation of neuroinflammatory, ER stress, apoptotic, and NMDAR2B-related pathways. These findings suggest that pantoprazole warrants further investigation as a potential adjunctive therapeutic strategy for epilepsy.
